{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABbZ0jpA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhE-VTI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 7, "title": "Deploy interactive MotionBricks SOMA demo to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions", "body": "## Goal

Publish the interactive MotionBricks + SOMA MVP demo from #5 as a **public, static GitHub Pages site**, automatically built and deployed via **GitHub Actions**.

Expected URL (once Pages is enabled and deployment succeeds): https://takahirox.github.io/three-motionbricks/

## Requirements

- [ ] Configure the demo for production/static hosting on GitHub Pages (Three.js + TypeScript; no mandatory backend).
- [ ] Add a GitHub Actions workflow (e.g. `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`) to install dependencies, build, upload the static site artifact, and deploy to GitHub Pages.
- [ ] Trigger deployment on push to `main` and support manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- [ ] Use the official GitHub Pages deployment actions (`configure-pages`, `upload-pages-artifact`, `deploy-pages`) and least-privilege permissions (`contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`), with sensible deployment concurrency.
- [ ] Correctly set the application base path to `/three-motionbricks/` and ensure built JS/CSS, model assets, and other resource URLs work under that subpath.
- [ ] Establish a practical strategy for the **large MotionBricks ONNX model** and SOMA character assets: avoid accidentally committing/licensing restricted assets or depending on unresolved Git LFS pointers in Pages output. If loading models remotely, verify hosting availability and CORS; document first-load download size, caching, and relevant licenses. Do not assume GitHub Pages can serve large model files reliably.
- [ ] Show a useful initialization/loading/error state, including a clear message when the browser lacks WebGPU support or model loading/inference fails.
- [ ] Document how to run the demo locally, how automatic deployment works, and any one-time repository setting needed (Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: **GitHub Actions**, if not already configured).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A push to `main` triggers the workflow and deploys successfully without manual build/upload steps.
- [ ] The public URL opens the demo over HTTPS without 404s for scripts, textures, character assets, or the ONNX model.
- [ ] On a supported WebGPU browser/GPU, the page runs the SOMA character and keyboard-driven MotionBricks locomotion delivered by #5.
- [ ] The deployed page handles missing WebGPU support and asset/network failures gracefully.
- [ ] README contains the public demo link, deployment steps, and any host/model-license caveats.

## Notes

- This is a **deployment/publishing task**; the implementation can include all GitHub Actions files and related configuration in the repository.
- Any GitHub Pages setting that cannot be changed by a workflow must be documented as a one-time manual setup step.
- Depends on #5 for the actual working interactive demo; workflow/site scaffolding may be implemented earlier.

## References

- MVP: #5
- [GitHub Pages custom workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages)
- [GitHub Pages deployment action](https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages)
